question: How does the apostle John establish the tangible, historical reality of the Incarnation of the Word of life?
opt1: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life
opt2: Through speculative philosophical hypotheses formulated in the intellectual academies of Alexandria
opt3: Through private allegorical dreams interpreted according to ancient oriental astrologies
opt4: Through mysterious nocturnal voices that forbade physical contact or sensory confirmation
correct: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life
explanation: John refutes proto-gnostic docetism by affirming that the eternal Word was personally heard, visually beheld, and physically touched by the apostles in real space and time. 1 John 1:1 (KJV) - "That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life;"

question: What eternal reality was manifested to the apostles, prompting their eyewitness testimony and proclamation to believers?
opt1: A temporary angelic phantom that dissolved without leaving any historical trace on earth
opt2: For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us
opt3: A code of ceremonial regulations intended to restore the national polity of the earthly Jerusalem
opt4: A secret gnosis reserved exclusively for an ascetic elite initiated into hidden mysteries
correct: For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us
explanation: The incarnate Christ is Himself eternal life personified, who eternally existed with the Father and was historically disclosed to the apostles for proclamation. 1 John 1:2 (KJV) - "(For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;)"

question: What is the supreme apostolic purpose in declaring that which they had seen and heard concerning Jesus Christ?
opt1: That ye may attain administrative authority over municipal civic assemblies across Asia Minor
opt2: That ye may construct monumental stone temples to rival the pagan sanctuaries of Ephesus
opt3: That ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ
opt4: That ye may enforce legal uniformity through civil litigation before Roman provincial magistrates
correct: That ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ
explanation: Apostolic preaching aims to invite believers into mutual spiritual communion, a sacred fellowship that shares directly in communion with the Father and His Son. 1 John 1:3 (KJV) - "That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ."

question: For what specific pastoral objective does John state that he writes these apostolic truths unto the church?
opt1: That your political dominance may be secured over secular governors
opt2: That your physical longevity may be multiplied beyond ancient patriarchs
opt3: That your financial revenues may increase through commercial monopolies
opt4: And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full
correct: And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full
explanation: The proclamation of fellowship with the Triune God is designed to bring the believers' spiritual joy to complete, overflowing fullness. 1 John 1:4 (KJV) - "And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full."

question: What foundational message concerning the divine nature did the apostles hear from Christ and declare unto believers?
opt1: That God is light, and in him is no darkness at all
opt2: That God is a complex balance between equal forces of moral light and darkness
opt3: That God remains an unknowable abyss indifferent to human righteousness and truth
opt4: That God changes His moral standards according to cultural developments among nations
correct: That God is light, and in him is no darkness at all
explanation: God's essential being is unadulterated holy light, completely devoid of moral imperfection, falsehood, or darkness. 1 John 1:5 (KJV) - "This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all."

question: What stark contradiction does John expose if someone claims fellowship with God while living in moral darkness?
opt1: We merely exhibit harmless personal eccentricities that do not impact our spiritual standing
opt2: If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth
opt3: We demonstrate high philosophical detachment from narrow moralistic definitions
opt4: We fulfill the secret purpose of divine grace through antinomian liberty
correct: If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth
explanation: Spiritual communion with a holy God cannot coexist with unrepentant walking in moral darkness; such a claim is both a verbal lie and a practical denial of truth. 1 John 1:6 (KJV) - "If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth:"

question: What two blessed spiritual realities occur when believers actively walk in the light as God is in the light?
opt1: We receive immediate worldly prosperity and immunity from physical sickness
opt2: We establish legislative dominance in civic courts and silence all secular critics
opt3: We have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin
opt4: We become worthy of salvation through our accumulated personal merits
correct: We have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin
explanation: Walking in the sphere of divine light produces authentic Christian community and ongoing purification through the atoning blood of Christ. 1 John 1:7 (KJV) - "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."

question: What fatal spiritual self-deception is revealed if anyone claims to be entirely without sin?
opt1: We demonstrate that we have achieved absolute angelic perfection on earth
opt2: We prove that we no longer need the written Scriptures for daily guidance
opt3: We manifest superior spiritual maturity that surpasses apostolic teaching
opt4: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us
correct: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us
explanation: Denying our sinful nature or moral failure is dangerous self-delusion, demonstrating the absence of divine truth in the heart. 1 John 1:8 (KJV) - "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us."

question: What glorious divine assurance is given to believers who sincerely confess their sins?
opt1: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness
opt2: If we conceal our sins, He will overlook them because of our financial contributions to the poor
opt3: If we confess our sins, He will impose severe penances before considering our pardon
opt4: If we deny our sins, He will validate our righteousness before angelic tribunals
correct: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness
explanation: God's forgiveness is rooted in His unwavering faithfulness and justice, satisfied by Christ's atonement, ensuring both pardon and cleansing to all who confess. 1 John 1:9 (KJV) - "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

question: What severe blasphemy and spiritual deficiency occur if someone asserts that they have never committed sin?
opt1: We simply express an alternative philosophical perspective without spiritual consequence
opt2: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us
opt3: We confirm that we are descendants of Abraham according to ancient genealogies
opt4: We demonstrate that our conscience is purely guided by Roman civil statutes
correct: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us
explanation: To deny having sinned contradicts God's universal verdict upon fallen humanity, effectively accusing God of lying and proving that His Word has no dwelling place within. 1 John 1:10 (KJV) - "If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us."

question: When a believer falls into sin, what divine provision and advocacy does John highlight before the Father?
opt1: We have an angelic mediator who petitions Michael the archangel to balance our good deeds against evil
opt2: We have a high priest from the line of Aaron who offers daily morning and evening incense at the altar
opt3: We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: and he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world
opt4: We must endure temporary purgatorial suffering until our personal merits satisfy divine justice
correct: We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: and he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world
explanation: Christ serves as our heavenly Advocate (Paraclete) whose righteous substitutionary atonement fully satisfies divine wrath for believers and extends sufficiency to the whole world. 1 John 2:1-2 (KJV) - "My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world."

question: How does John establish the definitive test of whether an individual truly possesses genuine experiential knowledge of God?
opt1: If we experience dramatic ecstatic visions and speak in secret uninterpretable tongues
opt2: If we master complex rabbinic genealogies and memorize philosophical paradoxes
opt3: If we donate substantial fortunes to civic magistrates to purchase church patronage
opt4: And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments
correct: And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments
explanation: Authentic saving knowledge of God is verified not by intellectual claims or mystical experiences, but by practical obedience to His moral commandments. 1 John 2:3 (KJV) - "And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments."

question: What moral standard is incumbent upon anyone who makes the profession of abiding in Christ?
opt1: He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked
opt2: Ought himself to withdraw into uninhabited mountain caves away from human society
opt3: Ought himself to enforce strict ceremonial washings before every meal
opt4: Ought himself to acquire prominent political office to govern secular citizens
correct: He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked
explanation: A profession of abiding in Christ obligates the believer to conform their daily conduct to the perfect moral example set by Jesus during His earthly walk. 1 John 2:6 (KJV) - "He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked."

question: How does John contrast the spiritual standing of one who loves his brother with one who harbors hatred toward a brother?
opt1: He that loveth his brother earns salvation by works, while he that hateth him merely requires theological instruction
opt2: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, but he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth
opt3: He that loveth his brother secures temporal riches, while he that hateth him incurs civic fines
opt4: He that loveth his brother follows Gentile customs, while he that hateth him preserves Jewish tradition
correct: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, but he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth
explanation: Love for fellow believers is the hallmark of walking in the light; conversely, hatred toward a brother exposes a soul blinded by moral and spiritual darkness. 1 John 2:10-11 (KJV) - "He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes."

question: Why does John address the young men in his threefold description of spiritual maturity within the Christian community?
opt1: Because ye possess superior physical athleticism and martial skill in defending assemblies
opt2: Because ye have amassed commercial fortunes to construct elaborate synagogues
opt3: Because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one
opt4: Because ye have mastered the oratorical dialectics of Greek philosophical schools
correct: Because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one
explanation: Young men in the faith represent spiritual vigor and victorious warfare against Satan, achieved because God's Word actively dwells within them. 1 John 2:14 (KJV) - "I have written unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one."

question: What three comprehensive worldly passions does John categorize as originating not from the Father, but from the fallen world?
opt1: The pursuit of agriculture, the engagement in honest trade, and the study of languages
opt2: The duty of civic taxation, the obedience to governors, and the practice of manual labor
opt3: The observance of dietary discipline, the marriage covenant, and the rearing of children
opt4: The lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
correct: The lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
explanation: John synthesizes worldliness into sensual appetites (lust of the flesh), materialistic covetousness (lust of the eyes), and arrogant self-exaltation (pride of life). 1 John 2:16 (KJV) - "For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world."

question: How does John contrast the transient nature of this present world with the permanent destiny of the obedient believer?
opt1: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever
opt2: The world evolves into an immortal utopia: while those who obey God vanish into nothingness
opt3: The world remains eternally immutable: while those who do God's will suffer perpetual reincarnations
opt4: The world belongs to the righteous by legal right: while sinners are exiled to distant planets
correct: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever
explanation: All worldly allurements and systems are ephemeral and decaying, whereas the person whose life is devoted to God's will participates in an everlasting destiny. 1 John 2:17 (KJV) - "And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever."

question: How does John explain the doctrinal departure of apostates who went out from the apostolic assembly?
opt1: They were forcibly expelled by Roman soldiers who raided the assembly during worship
opt2: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us
opt3: They were dispatched as official apostolic ambassadors to pioneer churches in distant territories
opt4: They departed merely because of linguistic misunderstandings regarding Hebrew idiom
correct: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us
explanation: Apostasy reveals an underlying absence of genuine regeneration; perseverance in sound fellowship is the mark of true belonging, whereas departure exposes spurious profession. 1 John 2:19 (KJV) - "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us."

question: How does John define the liar and the essential theological error of antichrist in 1 John 2:22?
opt1: He that refuses to observe circumcision and the ceremonial sabbath days
opt2: He that questions the chronology of the kings of Judah and Israel
opt3: Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son
opt4: He that fails to recite the Psalms from memory in the assembly
correct: Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son
explanation: The supreme theological lie is the denial of Jesus as the incarnate Christ, which severs relationship with both the Father and the Son. 1 John 2:22 (KJV) - "Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son."

question: What divine internal protection enables believers to discern spiritual truth and withstand deceptive teachers who seek to seduce them?
opt1: An imperial decree from Caesar forbidding heretical literature within the province
opt2: A secret cryptographic key handed down through pagan philosophical societies
opt3: A physical talisman blessed by the elders and worn around the neck
opt4: The anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things
correct: The anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things
explanation: The indwelling Holy Spirit (the divine unction/anointing) guides the regenerate believer into all truth, illuminating the apostolic gospel and safeguarding against heresy. 1 John 2:27 (KJV) - "But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him."

question: What magnificent manifestation of the Father's love is bestowed upon believers, and what ultimate transformation awaits at Christ's appearing?
opt1: That we should be called the sons of God: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is
opt2: That we should receive temporal empires on earth, and reign as mortal kings over pagan nations
opt3: That we should be transformed into winged seraphim, forgetting our earthly pilgrimage
opt4: That we should absorb the absolute divine essence, becoming sovereign creators of new universes
correct: That we should be called the sons of God: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is
explanation: God's lavish love adopts believers as His children now, with the glorious eschatological promise that when Christ appears, we will be conformed to His likeness through the beatific vision. 1 John 3:1-2 (KJV) - "Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is."

question: How does John define the fundamental essence of sin in 1 John 3:4, and what purifying effect does hope in Christ produce?
opt1: Sin is merely an illusion of unenlightened mortal thought that has no moral reality
opt2: Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure, for sin is the transgression of the law
opt3: Sin is the violation of human philosophical conventions and cultural traditions
opt4: Sin is an unavoidable physical destiny that cannot be overcome by divine grace
correct: Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure, for sin is the transgression of the law
explanation: Sin is lawlessness--the active violation of God's holy law; genuine hope in Christ motivates constant personal purification modeled on Christ's absolute purity. 1 John 3:3-4 (KJV) - "And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure. Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law."

question: For what explicit purpose was the Son of God manifested in human history according to 1 John 3:8?
opt1: That He might establish a geopolitical hegemony ruling from the city of Rome
opt2: That He might compromise with pagan mythologies to synthesize a universal world religion
opt3: For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil
opt4: That He might provide philosophical justification for continuing in fleshly indulgence
correct: For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil
explanation: Christ came not merely as an ethical teacher, but as the divine conqueror whose incarnation, death, and resurrection dismantle and annihilate the deceptive works of Satan. 1 John 3:8 (KJV) - "He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil."

question: Why cannot a person who is truly born of God persist in a habitual, unbroken lifestyle of sin?
opt1: Because an external angelic guard physically restrains his limbs from all movement
opt2: Because Roman civil magistrates threaten immediate execution for all moral offenses
opt3: Because he has taken a lifelong monastic vow in a consecrated desert monastery
opt4: For his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God
correct: For his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God
explanation: The new birth implants the divine seed--God's holy nature and indwelling Spirit--rendering persistent, unrepentant practice of sin incompatible with true regeneration. 1 John 3:9 (KJV) - "Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God."

question: What ancient Old Testament fratricide does John cite to illustrate the lethal malice of the devil against righteousness?
opt1: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous
opt2: Not as Esau, who sold his birthright for red pottage and wept bitter tears without repentance
opt3: Not as Absalom, who conspired against King David and perished when caught in an oak tree
opt4: Not as Korah, who rebelled against Aaron and was swallowed alive into the pit of the earth
correct: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous
explanation: Cain murdered Abel because his ungodly heart resented his brother's accepted, righteous sacrifice, symbolizing the world's hatred toward God's righteous children. 1 John 3:12 (KJV) - "Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous."

question: By what indisputable spiritual evidence do believers know that they have passed from death unto life?
opt1: Because we have acquired extensive property and wealth throughout Roman provinces
opt2: We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death
opt3: Because we recite lengthy liturgical creeds accurately in public assemblies
opt4: Because our names are engraved on monumental marble inscriptions in municipal forums
correct: We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death
explanation: Sincere, self-giving love for fellow Christians is the definitive evidence of having transitioned from spiritual death into eternal life. 1 John 3:14 (KJV) - "We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death."

question: How does John define the ultimate demonstration and standard of divine love in 1 John 3:16?
opt1: By accumulating emotional sympathy without taking any practical action to relieve suffering
opt2: By offering animal sacrifices at the temple altar during annual feast seasons
opt3: Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren
opt4: By composing poetic hymns celebrating sentimental human affection
correct: Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren
explanation: Love is known through Christ's voluntary substitutionary death on the cross, calling believers to an equivalent willingness to sacrifice themselves for the brethren. 1 John 3:16 (KJV) - "Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren."

question: How does John expose the hypocrisy of professing love only in words when a brother is in desperate material need?
opt1: Offer eloquent verbal blessings while referring the destitute brother to pagan charities
opt2: Deliver philosophical discourses on poverty while withholding material provisions
opt3: Instruct the hungry brother to fast continuously as an ascetic spiritual exercise
opt4: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth
correct: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth
explanation: Authentic Christian love cannot remain abstract rhetoric; it must prove itself through tangible generosity and active deeds that meet real needs. 1 John 3:17-18 (KJV) - "But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him? My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth."

question: What divine truth brings peace and assurance to believers when their sensitive hearts experience self-condemnation?
opt1: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things
opt2: God is indifferent to moral reality and never takes note of human actions
opt3: Our subjective feelings are infallible indicators of our eternal standing before God
opt4: Angelic intercessors can override divine omniscience and conceal our faults
correct: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things
explanation: God's infinite knowledge, grace, and sovereign covenant love surpass the flawed, fluctuating judgments of our subjective consciences. 1 John 3:20 (KJV) - "For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things."

question: What comprehensive twofold commandment does God give, and by what inner presence do we know He abides in us?
opt1: That we should observe the dietary code of Moses, and hereby we know by physical circumcisions
opt2: That we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another: and hereby we know that he abideth in us, by the Spirit which he hath given us
opt3: That we should offer gold to the temple treasury, and hereby we know by priestly certificates
opt4: That we should study Greek rhetoric, and hereby we know by rhetorical eloquence in debates
correct: That we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another: and hereby we know that he abideth in us, by the Spirit which he hath given us
explanation: God's commandment unites faith in Jesus Christ with fervent mutual love, confirmed inwardly by the presence and fruit of the Holy Spirit. 1 John 3:23-24 (KJV) - "And this is his commandment, That we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as he gave us commandment. And he that keepeth his commandments dwelleth in him, and he in him. And hereby we know that he abideth in us, by the Spirit which he hath given us."

question: By what cardinal theological test are believers instructed to try the spirits to discern whether they are of God?
opt1: Every spirit that performs dramatic signs and miracles before large crowds is of God
opt2: Every spirit that promises material wealth and political influence to followers is of God
opt3: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: and every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God
opt4: Every spirit that advocates strict vegetarian diets and ascetic solitude is of God
correct: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: and every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God
explanation: The critical doctrinal touchstone of divine inspiration is the confession of the true humanity and historical incarnation of the divine Son of God. 1 John 4:2-3 (KJV) - "Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world."

question: What empowering assurance enables believers to conquer false prophets and demonic spirits of error in the world?
opt1: Because you possess superior military weaponry to defend your assemblies from violence
opt2: Because Roman civil authorities have issued protective edicts safeguarding Christian doctrines
opt3: Because your intellectual eloquence can outwit pagan philosophers in public debates
opt4: Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world
correct: Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world
explanation: Believers are victorious over worldly deception because the indwelling power of the Holy Spirit is infinitely greater than Satan and all worldly forces combined. 1 John 4:4 (KJV) - "Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world."

question: On what fundamental divine attribute does John base the essential Christian duty of loving one another?
opt1: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love
opt2: Love is a cultural construct invented by philosophers to maintain civil tranquility
opt3: Love is an optional ascetic exercise for those seeking special monastic honours
opt4: Love is a legal transaction that requires monetary compensation before it is extended
correct: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love
explanation: Love originates in the very nature of God; because God is love, genuine regeneration inevitably produces a heart that reflects this divine essence. 1 John 4:7-8 (KJV) - "Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."

question: How was the supreme, initiatory love of God manifested toward fallen humanity according to 1 John 4:9-10?
opt1: By waiting until humanity attained moral perfection before extending divine mercy
opt2: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins
opt3: By granting earthly wealth and political power to patriarchal dynasties in Israel
opt4: By dispatching angelic hosts to destroy all who refused to keep the ceremonial law
correct: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins
explanation: True love did not originate from human devotion to God, but from God's gracious initiative in sending His Son as the atoning sacrifice (propitiation) for our sins. 1 John 4:9-10 (KJV) - "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."

question: Though no human being has seen God in His transcendent essence, how is His divine presence revealed and perfected in our midst?
opt1: Through monumental architectural temples built with gold and precious stones
opt2: Through elaborate theatrical dramas depicting mythological legends in public theaters
opt3: If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
opt4: Through political alliances forged with secular governors of imperial Rome
correct: If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
explanation: The invisible God becomes visible to the world through the loving community of believers, where His indwelling presence reaches its intended perfection. 1 John 4:12 (KJV) - "No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us."

question: What central saving truth do the apostles solemnly testify concerning the divine mission of Jesus Christ?
opt1: That the Father sent the Son to be an ordinary temporal king over the province of Judea
opt2: That the Father sent the Son to establish an exclusive scholastic academy in Athens
opt3: That the Father sent the Son to enforce ceremonial Levitical sacrifices throughout the earth
opt4: And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
correct: And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
explanation: The apostolic witness declares that the Father commissioned the Son with a universal redemptive mission to be the Savior of the world. 1 John 4:14 (KJV) - "And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world."

question: How does perfected divine love grant the believer fearless boldness in the impending day of judgment?
opt1: Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world
opt2: Because we have accumulated sufficient wealth to purchase exemption from divine scrutiny
opt3: Because we belong to an elite social caste that is immune to moral evaluation
opt4: Because we have performed rigorous bodily mortifications that cancel all future sin
correct: Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world
explanation: Believers face the judgment day with confidence because they share Christ's righteous standing and reflect His loving nature in this present world. 1 John 4:17 (KJV) - "Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world."

question: How does mature divine love conquer slavish fear and dread of condemnation in the believer?
opt1: Love embraces fear as a necessary spiritual torment to prove human unworthiness
opt2: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love
opt3: Love uses fear as an instrument to terrorize weaker brethren into submission
opt4: Love denies the existence of divine justice to create psychological tranquility
correct: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love
explanation: God's perfected love drives out paralyzing dread of punishment, replacing terror with deep filial peace and assurance in Christ. 1 John 4:18 (KJV) - "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love."

question: What is the foundational origin and source of all human love toward God according to 1 John 4:19?
opt1: We love Him because we recognized our intrinsic moral superiority over pagans
opt2: We love Him because we sought Him out through independent philosophical research
opt3: We love him, because he first loved us
opt4: We love Him because we were commanded by civil authorities under penalty of law
correct: We love him, because he first loved us
explanation: Human love for God is never self-generated or initial; it is a grateful, responsive adoration ignited solely by God's prior sovereign love toward us. 1 John 4:19 (KJV) - "We love him, because he first loved us."

question: What devastating exposure does John deliver against someone who claims to love God while hating a fellow Christian?
opt1: He is merely expressing a harmless emotional preference that God completely ignores
opt2: He demonstrates advanced theological acumen that rises above interpersonal relations
opt3: He is justified if the brother belongs to a different economic or social background
opt4: If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?
correct: If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?
explanation: It is spiritually impossible to love the invisible God while harboring malice toward a visible brother who bears God's image; such a claim is an outright lie. 1 John 4:20-21 (KJV) - "If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen? And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also."

question: How does John define the true love of God, and what is the victorious power that overcometh the world?
opt1: For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous. For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith
opt2: The love of God consists in mystical trances, and victory over the world is achieved through armed insurrections
opt3: The love of God is burdensome legalism, and victory over the world is secured through ascetic hermitage
opt4: The love of God is civic philanthropy, and victory over the world is won through commercial alliances
correct: For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous. For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith
explanation: Loving God is demonstrated by joyful, unburdensome obedience to His commandments, while regenerate faith is the supernatural instrument that triumphs over worldly allurements. 1 John 5:3-4 (KJV) - "For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous. For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith."

question: How did Jesus Christ come in historical reality, and what divine witness confirms this redemptive truth?
opt1: He came by water only at baptism, departing before the suffering of the cross, as false teachers allege
opt2: This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth
opt3: He came in mystical vision only, without entering into genuine physical human existence
opt4: He came with angelic chariots of fire to overturn Roman military garrisons
correct: This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth
explanation: Jesus was authenticated both at His baptism (water) and in His atoning sacrificial death (blood), confirmed by the Holy Spirit who is absolute truth. 1 John 5:6 (KJV) - "This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth."

question: According to 1 John 5:7-8 in the King James text, who are the witnesses that bear record in heaven and in earth?
opt1: Three that bear record in heaven, Abraham, Moses, and Elijah; and three on earth, Peter, James, and John
opt2: Three that bear record in heaven, Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael; and three on earth, kings, governors, and judges
opt3: Three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood
opt4: Three that bear record in heaven, the sun, the moon, and the stars; and three on earth, fire, air, and earth
correct: Three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood
explanation: The Trinitarian heavenly witnesses (Father, Word, Holy Ghost) are unified as one, complemented on earth by the converging witness of the Spirit, the water, and the blood. 1 John 5:7-8 (KJV) - "For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one."

question: What is the definitive divine record that God has testified concerning eternal life and His Son?
opt1: Eternal life is earned through flawless adherence to the traditions of the elders
opt2: Eternal life is distributed indiscriminately to all humanity regardless of their faith in Christ
opt3: Eternal life is an earthly heritage secured through physical descent from Abraham
opt4: God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life
correct: God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life
explanation: Eternal life is inextricably bound to the person of Jesus Christ; to possess the Son by faith is to have life, whereas to reject Him is to remain in spiritual death. 1 John 5:11-12 (KJV) - "And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life."

question: What is the primary stated purpose for which John wrote his first epistle to those who believe on the Son of God?
opt1: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life
opt2: That ye may construct elaborate liturgical manuals for episcopal synods
opt3: That ye may speculate about the secret numeric codes hidden in Hebrew genealogies
opt4: That ye may establish political dominion over municipal provincial assemblies
correct: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life
explanation: John wrote not to produce uncertainty or doubt, but to bestow conscious, unshakable assurance of eternal life upon all who place their trust in Jesus Christ. 1 John 5:13 (KJV) - "These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God."

question: What supreme confidence do believers possess when approaching God in petitionary prayer?
opt1: That if we repeat memorized incantations many times, God is compelled to grant selfish requests
opt2: That, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: and if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him
opt3: That God guarantees immediate fulfillment of all financial and material ambitions
opt4: That prayer is merely therapeutic meditation that never affects divine providence
correct: That, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: and if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him
explanation: Christian prayer is anchored in God's sovereign, revealed will; when petitions align with His will, believers can be utterly confident that God hears and answers. 1 John 5:14-15 (KJV) - "And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him."

question: In guiding believers concerning intercession for a brother who falls into sin, what distinction does John note?
opt1: Every sin committed after baptism automatically incurs instant physical and eternal death
opt2: Believers are prohibited from ever praying for any brother who commits any moral failure
opt3: If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death
opt4: All sins carry identical earthly penalties under apostolic church discipline
correct: If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death
explanation: Intercessory prayer brings life and restoration for sins not leading to death, while John acknowledges the solemn reality of high-handed apostate sin unto death. 1 John 5:16-17 (KJV) - "If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it. All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death."

question: What divine protection keeps the believer who is begotten of God from the devastating grasp of Satan?
opt1: He wears protective talismans and recites mystical apotropaic charms
opt2: He lives in an isolated fortress fortified against all outside communication
opt3: He purchases papal indulgences and certificates of absolution from elders
opt4: He that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not
correct: He that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not
explanation: The regenerate believer, empowered by Christ who preserves him, guards his spiritual life so that Satan cannot lay fatal hold upon his soul. 1 John 5:18 (KJV) - "We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not."

question: How does the apostle John identify Jesus Christ in the triumphant theological climax of his epistle?
opt1: And we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life
opt2: And we follow a created angelic being who attained divinity through moral effort
opt3: And we honour a mortal prophet whose tomb remains venerated in Galilee
opt4: And we acknowledge an earthly political deliverer who failed to overthrow Rome
correct: And we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life
explanation: In a climactic affirmation of Christ's full deity, John identifies Jesus Christ as the true God and eternal life in Himself. 1 John 5:20 (KJV) - "And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life."

question: With what concise, solemn apostolic warning does John conclude his first epistle to the elect children of God?
opt1: Little children, amass wealth for the impending famine. Amen.
opt2: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.
opt3: Little children, negotiate peace with Caesar's soldiers. Amen.
opt4: Little children, build monumental sanctuaries in every city. Amen.
correct: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.
explanation: John closes with an urgent, direct imperative to guard against all false gods, substitute loyalties, and spiritual counterfeits that rival exclusive devotion to Jesus Christ. 1 John 5:21 (KJV) - "Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen."
